title: Ephemeral KMS affinity and audit sanitization pipeline
author: Maya Singh
description:
Background: Customers operating in regulated regions asked for two pain points to be addressed together: (1) ensuring KMS usage is region-affine to tenant data residency policies, and (2) removing sensitive tokens and PII from downstream audit sinks prior to export. Motivation: previous work added KMS region scoping checks at the API surface, but key usage still flowed to global key wrappers in some paths and audit exporters occasionally leaked request-level tokens. This change bundles a defensive, production-ready approach: (A) an ephemeral KMS affinity layer that selects tenant-scoped, region-bound keys for short-lived operations and records deterministic key-tag metadata; (B) an audit-sanitization pipeline that applies attribute-aware redaction rules before any logs or audit events are published to external sinks.
What this PR does (concise):
- Adds a KMS Affinity evaluator (policy-driven) that resolves key candidates based on tenant attributes, data residency tag, and RBAC v2 attribute checks. The evaluator returns a short-lived key handle (ephemeral KMS token) and emits sealed metadata to the audit subsystem.
- Introduces an audit-sanitizer stage in the audit forwarder that: 1) removes bearer tokens and secrets from headers/metadata; 2) normalizes and redacts user-identifiable fields (email, phone, SSN-like patterns) using configurable regex rules; 3) annotates events with non-sensitive geotags (region-only).
- Adds RBAC v2 enforcement hooks so key selection requires the caller to possess both the key:use permission and the attribute:kms_region match for targeted tenants.
- Adds unit and integration tests for the affinity evaluator and sanitizer (including regression tests for previously-leaked path).
- Updates documentation (security/rbac.md and audit/exporter.md) and adds an operational guide for enabling sanitizer rules on a per-tenant basis.
Rollout plan: feature gated behind "security.ephemeral_kms_affinity" and "audit.sanitizer_v2" flags. Step 1: enable in staging and run log-compatibility job against internal sinks. Step 2: enable for a small set of low-volume tenants behind canary. Step 3: full rollout once metrics (no increased error rate, <0.1% sanitizer-induced drops) are green.
Checklist: - [x] Design doc: ENG-2145 linked - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test: local KMS emulator - [x] Docs updated - [x] Feature flags added - [x] Backwards-compatible by default (flags off)
Notes/Limitations: - The sanitizer uses heuristics for PII detection; customers with strict legal obligations should review rules and may opt to route raw audit streams to internal sinks only. - Ephemeral KMS tokens are short-lived (5m TTL) and rely on internal caching to avoid QPS spikes; autoscaling of the KMS proxy is included as an operator note in the rollout guide.

review_comments: Luca Patel: Can we avoid additional synchronous KMS round-trips on hot paths? Suggest returning a cached ephemeral handle when request TTL remains > 60s.
Author (Maya): Implemented caching layer in ephemeral_handle_manager with a kube-configurable ttl and max-stale window. See ephemeral_handle_manager.go (cache logic) and added unit tests.

Jordan Reyes: Sanitizer rules look good, but some regexes may be too aggressive — flagged potential false positives for order numbers. Please add allowlist exception for "order_id" patterns used in commerce flows.
Author (Maya): Added allowlist rules and a tenant-level override. Also added a test case that simulates commerce payloads.
Priya Verma: Need to ensure RBAC audit trail includes the attribute match that permitted key selection. Otherwise downstream reviewers can't verify region affinity.
Author (Maya): Audit event now contains a sealed 'kms_affinity_metadata' blob (non-sensitive) with region tag and policy hash. Confirmed no secret material is leaked.
ci_notes: Initial CI run failed due to flaky metrics test (metrics/integration::TestSanitizerLatency). Reran job after test isolation fix; all checks passed. Added staging-only compatibility job to prevent future regressions.
release_notes: Security: Add tenant-scoped ephemeral KMS affinity and an audit-sanitizer pipeline. Operators can enable via feature flags; mitigates accidental export of tokens/PII and enforces region-bound key usage for regulated tenants.
operational_impact: Deploys a new KMS proxy sidecar (optional) and a sanitizer stage in the audit forwarder. Operators should review autoscaling guidance; follow the rollout steps in docs/audit/exporter.md.
qa_steps: 1) Run local-kms-emulator and sanity-check affinity resolution for tenant A (US) and tenant B (EU). 2) Send synthetic requests containing bearer tokens and PII to audit forwarder and verify sanitized output. 3) Enable feature flags in staging and run compatibility job. 4) Monitor sanitizer drop-rate and KMS proxy latency in staging for 24h.
notes_for_support: If tenants report missing audit fields after enabling the sanitizer, check tenant-level allowlist and sanitation rules. Support can temporarily disable sanitizer for that tenant via the feature flag until rules are updated.
security_considerations: All ephemeral handles are issued with limited scopes and TTL. The sanitizer strips tokens before export and replaces values with redaction markers. Audit metadata exposes only non-secret attributes (region, policy-hash).
human_summary: Implements policy-driven ephemeral KMS selection tied to tenant region and an audit sanitization stage that redacts PII and tokens before exporting logs; includes tests, docs, and an operator rollout plan.
